Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Partnership: PromptWorks SDK + Redwood connectors (LlamaIndex/LangChain)

Hi Marissa,

Hope you're doing well — I'm Jamie, Head of Integrations at PromptWorks (we build prompt tooling, prompt-versioning, and an SDK used by LlamaIndex and LangChain communities). We've been seeing customers asking for a first-class Redwood connector so they can route generation/cost controls through your runtime while using our SDK for prompt orchestration and tracing.

High-level ask: would Redwood be interested in a joint integration (connector + tracing hooks + a sample reference app) and a co-marketing launch? We think the win is twofold: (1) PromptWorks customers get predictable inference economics via Redwood and (2) Redwood gets better upstream SDK adoption.

I can share a short integration spec and a demo repo if that helps. If you prefer, I'd love to set a quick 30-min tech sync next week.

Best,
Jamie Liu
Head of Integrations, PromptWorks
jamie@promptworks.io
+1 (415) 555-0198

Hi all — quick technical note ahead of the sync. Thanks for the outreach, Jamie. A few things we'll want clarity on so we can scope the connector and tracing integration: 

1) Auth model: do you expect customers to call PromptWorks SDK which then calls Redwood API directly with their key, or do you want PromptWorks to proxy calls through a partner account owned by PromptWorks (token exchange / brokered credentials)?

2) Tracing hooks: what events do you expect? (prompt.start, prompt.end, token.count, model.variant) — we have runtime hooks for token-level metrics and can emit trace spans to OpenTelemetry or to your tracing endpoint.

3) Prompt tooling features: do you rely on LlamaIndex's index serialization or LangChain agents for routing? That will affect the connector surface (streaming vs batch vs chain-of-tools).

4) Data residency / PII: any special requirements from your customers (we support VPC/private deployments and can ensure bypassing hosted logs if needed).

I've attached a short draft integration guide (integration-guide-draft.pdf) with our recommended connector API shape (REST + streaming websocket fallback) and a minimal set of trace fields. 

For the sync, Tue 2/17 11am PST works for me; if that works for you too Jamie, I'll send a calendar invite and include a short agenda (tech scope + milestones + artifact list + owners).

Cheers,
Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: integration-guide-draft.pdf

Subject: Re: Partnership: PromptWorks SDK + Redwood connectors (LlamaIndex/LangChain)

Thanks Dev — this is helpful. Quick answers inline:

1) Auth model: we prefer the "customer-owned key" approach — PromptWorks SDK will let customers configure a Redwood API key so calls go direct-to-Redwood (no brokered credentials). For enterprise customers that require brokered flows we can support a token-exchange path (we have an existing exchange pattern).

2) Tracing hooks: yes to the list you proposed. We emit spans for prompt.start/prompt.end and token counts; we can map those to OpenTelemetry resource attributes. We'll also support an optional "annotation" field for prompt_version and prompt_template_id.

3) Prompt tooling: most of our early users use LlamaIndex for retrieval + LangChain for chains. The connector should support streaming completions and a batch-mode inference call for synchronous embedding/rr tasks.

4) Data residency: no extra PII needs for our demo customers; enterprise integrations will have their own contracts.

I'll drop our connector schema (promptworks-connector-v1.yaml) into the repo and share a short demo link. Looking forward to the sync tomorrow at 11am PST.

Jamie
Head of Integrations, PromptWorks
Attachment: promptworks-connector-v1.yaml

- Connector will support streaming completions + batch inference endpoints
- Tracing: PromptWorks will emit OTel spans; Redwood will accept spans and link to request ids for cost/latency per-call reporting

- Legal/Procurement: Mateo will draft a short SOW and partner agreement; using SOW-template.docx as baseline (Mateo) — target 2026-03-04

I've attached our SOW template and will open a HubSpot deal (PW-2026-042). Mateo — can you take the SOW draft? Jamie — once you publish the connector repo link, please post to the shared GitHub URL and we'll reference it in the launch plan.

Thanks — excited to partner on this.
